extracted.intended_audience: Practitioners before the USPTO (patent attorneys, patent agents, trademark attorneys), their staff (paralegals/assistants), and OED/Opla staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on professional responsibility and disciplinary standards for practitioners before the USPTO, describing types of misconduct, examples, regulatory bases for discipline, and procedural resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal disciplinary sanctions (public discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal discipline, with a few exceptions, constitutes public discipline; disciplinary sanctions include exclusion from practice before the Office; suspension from practice before the Office; reprimand or censure; or probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a). These are the primary formal sanctions OED may impose; formal discipline is generally public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warnings vs. formal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may conclude an investigation with a warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A warning is neither public nor a disciplinary sanction. Cites 37 C.F.R. § 11.21.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline imposed based on discipline by a state or federal program or agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually conducted on a documentary record only. Cites 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension for conviction of serious crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension may be imposed based on conviction of a serious crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a mechanism for immediate suspension pending further proceedings. Cites 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest / concurrent representation without agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Representing multiple clients (e.g., joint inventors) without a written agreement and continuing representation despite disputes between clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In re Radanovic — continued to represent two inventors without written agreement, then abandoned application naming both in favor of one; resulted in public reprimand. Mitigating factors (e.g., long clean disciplinary history) may affect sanction severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect / failure to manage client matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglecting client matters (e.g., failing to monitor communications and deadlines) resulting in abandoned applications or expired patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: In re Frantz (neglected dozens of matters; allowed applications to go abandoned without informing clients — exclusion); In re Tachner (failed to report Office communications/due dates, used inadequate docketing methods, undertrained staff — 5-year suspension). Highlights duty to maintain effective docketing and trained staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in dishonest acts such as misappropriation of funds, submitting false financial reports, falsely representing filings, creating fake filing receipts or letters, and billing for services not performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: In re Reardon (misappropriated nonprofit funds; excluded from practice), In re Goldstein (fabricated filings and communications; excluded). Sanctions range from public reprimand and probation to exclusion from practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to supervise non-lawyer assistants
rubrics_metrics.description: Inadequate supervision of non-lawyer assistants who fabricate filings or communications or sign attorney's signature to filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In re Druce — assistant fabricated filings and communications and signed attorney's signature; attorney received a stayed suspension and probation upon reinstatement. Proper supervision of staff is required to avoid discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized ex parte communication with adjudicator/tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: Contacting a judge or tribunal (e.g., PTAB judge) without copying/opposing counsel or appropriate authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In re Caracappa — subordinate authorized to email PTAB judge without copying opposing counsel; resulted in public reprimand. Avoid unilateral communications with adjudicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: False submissions and failure to correct (Rule 131 / declarations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing declarations or statements that are later discovered to be inaccurate and failing to advise the Office in writing of the inaccuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In re Tendler — filed a Rule 131 declaration later found inaccurate and did not notify the Office; resulted in a 4-year suspension for conduct prejudicial to administration of justice. Practitioners must correct known inaccuracies promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abusive or unprofessional communications with judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in abusive conduct toward judges (e.g., leaving abusive voicemail messages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: In re Tassan — left abusive voicemails for TTAB judges; received public reprimand and was ordered to complete anger management course. Maintain professional demeanor in all communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure and candor to the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation to disclose confidential client information that is material to patentability, manage representations when concurrent litigation and prosecution exist, and make truthful representations when evidence is conflicting or incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes considerations around protective orders and assessing representations in light of incomplete/conflicting evidence. Failure to satisfy duty of candor may result in discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized filings (by unauthorised parties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings made by parties not authorized to act on behalf of an applicant (e.g., unauthorized assignment documents, express abandonments, IDS filings, or corrections of inventorship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Trademark cases — unauthorized assignment/express abandonment; Patent cases — unauthorized assignment documents, information disclosure statements, or inventorship corrections. Ensure filings are authorized by proper parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication with client regarding imminent deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling situations where a response due date is approaching and the client has not explicitly authorized action (or inaction); also addressing receipt of incomplete filings and determining whether they were intentionally incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must verify authorization from the client before acting or allowing abandonment; must investigate incomplete filings to determine intent and protect client interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding unauthorized practice of law by staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Preventing paralegals or assistants from performing tasks that constitute the unauthorized practice of law (e.g., taking substantive calls from examiners, advising clients about legal strategy, or contacting PTO about application issues without attorney oversight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: examiner calls taken by paralegals/assistants; clients contacting paralegals about application substance; paralegals calling PTO with application questions. Attorneys must control delegation and ensure only authorized persons provide legal advice or undertake lawyer-only tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing and using public disciplinary decisions and official notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to find decisions imposing public discipline (FOIA Reading Room) and Official Gazette notices for patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) — select 'Discipline' in Decision Type and click 'Get Info' to retrieve discipline cases. Official Gazette for Patents available at http://www.uspto.gov/news/og/patent_og/index.jsp (select issue and 'Notices'). Useful for research and precedent when assessing disciplinary outcomes.
